title: Why this Texas recruit chose Utah football over Northwestern, Baylor and Houston
text:
Why this 3-star recruit from Texas felt at home with Utah football 
 Why this Texas recruit chose Utah football over Northwestern, Baylor and Houston
 The Utes won over Darrod Jacobs with a family feel. Now he is ready to get to work.
 (Per Darrod Jacobs) Utah three-star recruit Darrod Jacobs lines up as he prepares to defend for Port Arthur Memorial High School in Texas.
 By  Jason Batacao  | Oct. 30, 2026, 6:00 a.m. | Updated: 8:57 a.m. Comment
 Add as Preferred Source
 Darrod Jacobs didn’t know much about the University of Utah before he received the call his junior year. 
 But he did know one thing: It’s where Chicago Bears corner Clark Phillips III played collegiately.
 “I didn’t know anything beyond that, to be honest,” Jacobs, a three-star recruit from Port Arthur Memorial High School in Port Arthur, Texas, told The Salt Lake Tribune. 
 That wasn’t a bad place to start. 
 Phillips — who tied the Utah school record with six pick-6s before he entered the NFL draft in 2023 — is a pretty good starting point, especially since cornerbacks coach and associate head coach Sharrieff Shah is Jacobs’ primary recruiter.
 Jacobs’ relationship with Shah ultimately led him to commit to the U. over Northwestern, North Texas, Baylor and Houston. 
 “He’s real energetic,” Jacobs said of Shah. “Anytime he calls me, he’s always suped up, ready to talk. We talked for an hour one night about football and family.”
 Those football talks usually revolve around the player Jacobs could become when he gets to campus in the coming months.

 Football and family have long been part of the Utes’ recruiting mantra.
 That became clear for Jacobs during his official visit on May 29, during which he spent time with coaches and players, including quarterback Byrd Ficklin and running back LaMarcus Bell.
 The way the players and coaches interacted left a strong impression on Jacobs.
 “What stuck out to me is the player-coach relationships they have,” Jacobs said. “On my OV, I was watching and seeing how the players moved.”
 “And it wasn’t just the regular player and coach conversations that they were having. It was son and dad’s conversation — if you know what I’m saying.”
 Soon, he was committed to the school a little over 1,500 miles away. 
 “I never expected that I’d be a Ute right now,” Jacobs said. “But I’m glad I am, though.”
 And he’s ready to get going. 
 Jacobs hopes to eventually join the long list of Utah defensive backs who have landed in the NFL. 
 “When I touch down on campus, it’s grind time,” he said. “I don’t know how else to put it. I have to get to the top.”
